claim: Ridge regression is solved in O~(r*sqrt(mn)/epsilon + n^3) quantum time versus O~(mr + poly(n,1/epsilon)) classically (Corollary 25).
paper: Accelerating Regression Tasks with Quantum Algorithms (arXiv:2509.24757 / OpenReview TBSyYj4VV6)
method: Leverage-score sparsifier; ridge optimum on sketch vs full; m-scaling timed; asymptotic symbolic.
reason: Ridge optimum preserved on sparsifier: loss_ratio=0.001<=0.15, gram rel-err=0.111<=0.15 (strongly-convex -> theoretical (1+/-eps) guarantee). Classical ridge solve slope in m = 1.34, sketch slope = -1.48. Quantum/classical -> 0 as m->inf. EVIDENCE BOUNDARY: literal quantum construction (QRAM) NOT executed on CPU; shown via classical surrogate + symbolic limit.

mutation.description: (M1) s<r/eps^2 breaks optimum-preservation; (M2) tighter eps needs more samples; (M3) quantum sqrt(m) required for speedup.
